gloss: vinyl sheet; plastic tarp; ground sheet

definitions.gloss: vinyl sheet; plastic tarp; ground sheet
definitions.explanation: A large flat piece of vinyl or plastic material used as a ground cover, protective sheet, or tarp. Commonly used for picnics, outdoor events, construction sites, and disaster preparedness.

examples.japanese: ビニールシートを{敷|し}いて{座|すわ}った。
examples.english: We spread out a vinyl sheet and sat down.

examples.japanese: {花見|はなみ}のために{大|おお}きなビニールシートを{持|も}っていった。
examples.english: I brought a large plastic sheet for the cherry blossom viewing.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}に{備|そな}えて、{屋根|やね}をビニールシートで{覆|おお}った。
examples.english: In preparation for the typhoon, we covered the roof with a vinyl tarp.

notes:
A wasei-eigo (Japanese-English compound) from ビニール (vinyl) + シート (sheet). In English, the closest equivalents are "tarp," "ground sheet," or "plastic sheet" depending on the context. The blue vinyl tarps (ブルーシート) seen at construction sites and disaster areas are the most iconic type.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ビニールシートを{敷|し}く: to spread out a vinyl sheet
- ビニールシートで{覆|おお}う: to cover with a vinyl sheet
- ビニールシートを{張|は}る: to stretch/put up a tarp
- {防水|ぼうすい}ビニールシート: waterproof vinyl sheet

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, ビニールシート is closely associated with {花見|はなみ} (cherry blossom viewing) and other outdoor gatherings. People spread blue sheets under trees to claim spots in parks. At construction sites and after natural disasters, blue tarps (ブルーシート) are ubiquitous.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ブルーシート: blue tarp — the standard blue construction/emergency tarp
- {敷|し}き{物|もの}: ground covering — more general term for anything laid on the ground
- レジャーシート: leisure sheet — specifically for recreational outings
